mathematical_review: A_n increase because 1/n decreases, and each x in K has |x|>0 so lies in some A_n. Each A_n is relatively closed, hence Borel; sigma-algebra differences make B_n Borel. The B_n are disjoint with union K. Countable additivity gives a nonnegative sum equal to one, forcing at least one positive term. B_n is contained in A_n, and the disjoint split of A_n gives P(A_n)>=P(B_n)>0. The existing simple-function refinement estimate is uniform below s0 for this fixed P; the two-point mean-zero measures approach s0. Thus the complete bounded positive continuous concave-extension counterexample and its entropy units are preserved.
